{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Edward Snowden’s revelations of the National Security Agency’s extraordinarily pervasive invasion of privacy rights should have triggered an equally far-reaching debate over the proper balance between needs for liberty and security.",
"claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Too many democratic freedoms have already been sacrificed on the altar of a never ending “war on terrorism”.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The term “war” exaggerates the real level of threat that terrorism poses.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The use of the term “war” enables the government to deploy rhetoric to justify unnecessary restrictions on civil liberties.",
"claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The Obama administration has focused on a vindictive hunt to arrest and punish the whistleblower.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"The Evo Morales plane incident demonstrates that the conduct of the hunt to arrest and punish the whistleblower is damaging America’s international reputation.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Snowden’s revelations that the NSA was spying on governments allied to the USA on matters not remotely related to security against terrorism is damaging America’s international reputation.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Acting on an unfounded report that the diplomatic plane carrying Bolivian President Evo Morales was spiriting Edward Snowden to asylum caused several European governments allied to the USA to deny routine overflight and refueling rights.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Denial of overflight and refueling rights resulted in what President Morales called a virtual kidnapping.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Several other elected Latin American leaders have joined Morales in denouncing the denial of overflight and refueling rights as imperialist and colonialist.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"The French president has apologized for the denial of overflight and refueling rights.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"The leaders of Spain, Portugal, Italy and the USA have not apologized for the denial of overflight and refueling rights.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]}],"unresolved_references":[]}

{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Edward Snowden’s revelations of the National Security Agency’s extraordinarily pervasive invasion of privacy rights should have triggered an equally far-reaching debate over the proper balance between our needs for liberty and for security.",
"claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Too many of our precious democratic freedoms have already been sacrificed on the altar of a never ending “war on terrorism”.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The term “war” exaggerates the real level of threat that terrorism poses.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The use of the term “war” enables our government to deploy the rhetoric of “war” to justify unnecessary restrictions on our civil liberties.",
"claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The Obama administration has focused on a vindictive hunt to arrest and punish the whistleblower.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"The Evo Morales plane incident demonstrates that the conduct of this frantic quest to arrest and punish the whistleblower is damaging America’s international reputation as much as Snowden’s revelations that the NSA was spying on governments allied to the USA on matters not remotely related to security against terrorism.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Snowden’s revelations that the NSA was spying on governments allied to the USA on matters not remotely related to security against terrorism is damaging America’s international reputation.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Acting on an unfounded report that the diplomatic plane carrying Bolivian President Evo Morales was spiriting Edward Snowden to asylum caused several European governments allied to the USA to deny routine overflight and refueling rights.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Denial of routine overflight and refueling rights resulted in what President Morales called a virtual kidnapping.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Several other elected Latin American leaders have joined Morales in denouncing these flagrant violations of international law and practice as imperialist and colonialist.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"The French president has apologized, but not the leaders of Spain, Portugal, Italy or the USA.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[4]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
